title: Welcome to Tennessee!
fact: Tennessee is the Volunteer State. Its flag has 3 stars for East, Middle and West!

title: The Tennessee Flag
fact: Color the flag: red, white and blue. The 3 stars stand for East, Middle and West Tennessee!

title: Memphis
fact: Ducks march to a fountain at Memphis's Peabody Hotel every day!

title: Tiptonville
fact: Earthquakes in 1811 and 1812 made Reelfoot Lake. Cypress trees grow in the water!

title: Paris
fact: Paris, Tennessee has its own 70-foot Eiffel Tower!

title: Jackson
fact: Famous train engineer Casey Jones lived in Jackson!

title: Clarksville
fact: Olympic star Wilma Rudolph grew up here and won 3 gold medals in 1960!

title: Nashville
fact: Nashville has a full-size copy of the Parthenon from Greece!

title: Franklin
fact: Franklin's historic downtown has a movie theater that opened in 1937!

title: Columbia
fact: Columbia hosts Mule Day every spring with a big parade!

title: Murfreesboro
fact: Murfreesboro was the capital of Tennessee from 1818 to 1826!

title: Cookeville
fact: Cummins Falls near Cookeville tumbles 75 feet. You can see lots of waterfalls here!

title: Chattanooga
fact: The Incline Railway up Lookout Mountain is one of the steepest in the world!

title: Sweetwater
fact: The Lost Sea in Sweetwater is America's largest underground lake!

title: Oak Ridge
fact: In the 1940s Oak Ridge was a secret city. Today scientists there use super computers!

title: Knoxville
fact: The Sunsphere is a gold glass ball 266 feet tall, built for the 1982 World's Fair!

title: Sevierville
fact: A statue of singer Dolly Parton sits at the courthouse. She grew up nearby!

title: Pigeon Forge
fact: Dollywood in Pigeon Forge has roller coasters and a real steam train!

title: Gatlinburg
fact: Gatlinburg is the door to the Great Smoky Mountains, America's most-visited national park!

title: Johnson City
fact: Scientists dug up animal fossils about 5 million years old at the Gray Fossil Site!

title: Kingsport
fact: Bays Mountain Park in Kingsport has a planetarium for looking at the stars!

title: Bristol
fact: Bristol sits in two states! Its main street is part Tennessee, part Virginia.

title: My Family's Town
fact: My family is from ________. Draw your family inside the frame!

title: Goodbye, Tennessee!
fact: Scout visited 20 towns in East, Middle and West Tennessee. Which was your favorite?
